name: capability-promotion-registry
purpose: Defines the bounded black-box process for detecting repeated work, bottlenecks, omissions, and manual rework, generating improvement ideas, evaluating those ideas, then promoting selected ideas into the smallest reusable platform capability.

reader_guide.summary: Open this file when the platform should improve itself while work is happening. User-facing automation may feel black-box-like, but every observation, candidate, risk decision, validation, rollback path, and promotion result must remain auditable.
how_to_read: Read platform_principle before interpreting this as full autonomy.
Use observation_sources and promotion_triggers to decide whether a recurring pattern is real.
Use idea_generation and idea_evaluation_rubric to create several candidate ideas and score them before promotion.
Use capability_types to choose the smallest reusable asset.
Use risk_tiers and autonomy_limits before applying changes.
Use promotion_pipeline and required_records to close the loop with validation, evaluation, documentation, commit, and push.
update_triggers: The platform starts creating prompts, workflows, templates, tools, skills, agents, or project features from observed work patterns.
Repeated friction, bottleneck, omission, validation failure, or manual rework rules change.
Automatic capability promotion risk tiers or human checkpoint rules change.
Capability idea generation, scoring criteria, pass thresholds, or rejection reasons change.
A new reusable capability type is added.
A monitor, desktop app, or orchestration layer starts showing capability candidates or promotion status.

structure_rules.rule: The user-facing flow may feel automatic, but the platform must not hide internal observations, candidate decisions, risks, validation, rollback, or promotion records.
structure_rules.reason: Autonomous self-improvement without traceability creates hallucination, maintenance, and accountability risk.

structure_rules.rule: Promote repeated work to the smallest useful asset before creating a heavier agent or project feature.
structure_rules.reason: The platform should reduce repetitive work without creating unnecessary maintenance burden.

structure_rules.rule: Promotion candidates need at least one concrete observation source and a predicted reduction in time, repetition, omission risk, or validation friction.
structure_rules.reason: The platform should not generate features from vague preference alone.

structure_rules.rule: Capability promotion must separate idea generation from idea evaluation; no idea can be promoted until it has explicit scores, evaluator notes, a decision, and rejection or queue reasons for alternatives.
structure_rules.reason: Automatic feature creation should produce several options and select through visible criteria instead of treating the first generated idea as the answer.

structure_rules.rule: Destructive, secret-bearing, permission-changing, install, paid, public-release, security, privacy, irreversible migration, or ownership-boundary changes require a human checkpoint before execution.
structure_rules.reason: Self-improving automation must keep owner authority over high-impact actions.

structure_rules.rule: Every applied capability promotion must define validation and rollback or disablement before it is marked complete.
structure_rules.reason: Self-created platform capabilities should be reversible and testable.

field_guide.meaning: Plain-language principle for bounded autonomous platform improvement.
Repository records the agent can inspect to discover repeated work and bottlenecks.
Signals that allow a candidate capability to be proposed.
Rules for generating multiple improvement ideas from observed signals before selecting a candidate.
Scoring dimensions, thresholds, and decision outcomes for evaluating generated ideas before promotion.
Allowed reusable assets and their target directories and validation requirements.
Ordered process for turning observations into validated reusable capabilities.
Records that must exist before promotion can be considered complete.
Actions the platform must not execute automatically.

platform_principle: The platform may automate capability discovery and candidate drafting, but it must remain transparent, testable, reversible, and owner-controlled. It should feel automatic to the user only because the boring discovery and bookkeeping are handled, not because decisions become invisible.

generation_rules: Generate more than one way to reduce the observed repetition or bottleneck when the problem is not trivial.
Include at least one lighter-weight option before proposing a tool, skill, agent, or project feature.
Include a do-nothing or defer option when the signal may be too weak.
Do not generate ideas that require high-risk execution without labeling the human checkpoint.

dimensions.meaning: How much repeated human work this idea removes.
How much elapsed or active work time this idea can plausibly reduce.
How small and maintainable the idea remains after implementation; lower maintenance burden scores higher.
How well the idea is supported by observed records, user requests, tests, external references, or evaluator history.
Whether the idea's risk tier, human checkpoint, and rollback path match the expected benefit.
Whether the idea uses the smallest suitable capability type rather than overbuilding.

promotion_triggers.condition: The same manual sequence appears at least twice or is expected to recur across projects.
promotion_triggers.default_action: Create a prompt, workflow, or template candidate.

promotion_triggers.condition: A timing record or evaluator note identifies a slow phase that can be reduced by deterministic execution or better routing.
promotion_triggers.default_action: Create a tool, workflow, or monitor enhancement candidate.

promotion_triggers.condition: Omission, grounding, config, spec, resource, or evaluation checks repeatedly fail for the same reason.
promotion_triggers.default_action: Create a guardrail, checklist, evaluator, or workflow candidate.

promotion_triggers.condition: The same domain-specific judgment rules need to be remembered across sessions.
promotion_triggers.default_action: Create a skill or agent candidate.

promotion_triggers.condition: A recurring platform operation would be easier from UI, desktop app, or monitor surface.
promotion_triggers.default_action: Create a project feature candidate with UX, risk, and validation notes.

capability_types.use_when: The repeated work is judgment framing or a reusable instruction sequence.
The repeated work has ordered steps and close-out requirements.
The repeated value is structure, not execution.
The repeated work is deterministic execution, conversion, validation, indexing, scoring, or generation.
The repeated work is agent behavior, domain rules, or tool integration knowledge that Codex should load on demand.
The repeated work needs explicit input/output contracts, tools, policy, validation, and orchestration metadata.
The repeated work belongs in a product surface, monitor, desktop app, or project-specific module.
validation: UI or artifact verification when applicable

risk_tiers.autonomy: May be drafted and applied when repository rules, validation, and rollback are clear.

examples: new local tool without new dependencies
risk_tiers.autonomy: May be implemented after requirements/spec/evaluation gates in governance mode.
Requires human checkpoint, rollback plan, and dedicated audit record before execution.

autonomy_limits: Do not auto-run destructive file, git, database, or infrastructure changes.
Do not auto-add or expose secrets, tokens, credentials, or private data.
Do not auto-install, upgrade, remove, or globally configure software without installation audit and human checkpoint when risk is high.
Do not auto-enable paid services, external publishing, public deployment, or permission changes.
Do not auto-promote a capability when a lighter existing asset already solves the observed problem.
Do not treat repeated LLM agreement as factual proof; use sources, tests, tools, evaluators, or human judgment.
